label: Late original phase / <DEL> step, mainly in sequences starting with z (or 1, r, p, f, 2)
explanation: Fires only at steps t>=3 of the original phase and at the <DEL> step (99% of mass). It peaks at orig_idx 5-6 and is about 25% likely at <DEL>. It is almost silent in the copy phase, apart from weak firing at recall_idx 1, and never fires at t<3. Within that window, whether it fires depends on the early tokens of the sequence. Rates are highest when the first original token is z (4.4x lift; the top examples all start with z z), followed by 1, r, p, f and 2, or when z is the second token. Magnitude is also highest in z-initial sequences. Gating on the window alone gives recall 0.99 but precision only about 0.21. Adding the first-token condition gives dev F1 0.54 and mass recall 0.66, so the token-content dependence is only partly captured and looks like a graded hidden-state feature.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: z, 1, r, p, f, 2; least: y, d, v, a) and the second original token (most: z, o, 3, x, 2, 1; least: q, d, y, a); timing cues that raise it most: t=5, t=6, recall_idx=1.
